solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Still laborious lassoing horse

indicators.note: a lasso loops right round what it catches, so one piece encircles the other

blocks.note: tough work is laborious work
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A cowboy finds roping a horse hard going while standing motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adjective meaning motionless, but it is the adverb meaning nevertheless; horse and H are both slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: As a sentence adverb meaning nevertheless or however, the word replaces 'still' exactly: 'it rained; it was fun, though'.

clue.text: Chest picked up by crew reportedly in dock?

indicators.note: a sound picked up is caught by the ear, so we work from how it is heard
something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by the sound

blocks.note: a trunk is a large storage chest
a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Sailors lifting a sea chest in the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk eight', said quickly, gives the answer. The question mark flags that 'dock' is the verb meaning cut short, not the harbour the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock a tail or wages is to cut it short, which is exactly what shortening by lopping off an end means.

clue.text: Trot raised in Paris suburb becomes attendant

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting letters up makes them read from bottom to top
one thing sitting in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: a Trot, a Trotskyist, is a left-winger or red
Orly, home of the airport, is a suburb south of Paris

explanation.surface: A horse's trot being practised in a suburb of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trot' looks like a horse's gait but is short for Trotskyist, a common crossword route to RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital orderly is an attendant who carries out non-medical tasks such as moving patients.

clue.text: Giant fish a month back devouring worker?

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so these letters read in reverse
whatever devours something takes it inside itself

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted freshwater fish
Aug is the abbreviation for August
a worker ant; the question mark admits the example

explanation.surface: A huge fish swallowing a worker, as if a month ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' only gives 'a month' its surface sense; the month is AUG. The reversed month then swallows the worker after the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantua is the enormous giant of Rabelais's satire, whose name gave English the word gargantuan.

clue.text: Drug taken by doctor — former PM almost ready for fight

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: E is ecstasy
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
Clement Attlee was UK Prime Minister 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: A doctor hands drugs to a one-time prime minister spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the Labour prime minister after the Second World War; clipping his name leaves ATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To embattle is to prepare troops or defences for battle, so 'ready for fight' works as a verb phrase.

clue.text: Grower to celebrate extraordinary green trade

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of its usual form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to mark an anniversary is to celebrate it
taken as written, ready to be reworked

explanation.surface: A grower celebrating a remarkable boom in eco-friendly business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green trade' sounds like an environmental phrase, and fits a grower neatly, but it is just the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A market gardener raises vegetables and fruit commercially, so is a grower by occupation.

clue.text: University supporting article on little woman in duchy once

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece is placed below the others

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
Jo March is one of Alcott's Little Women
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university backing an article about a small woman in an old French province.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' means placed underneath, so the university letter comes last. 'Little woman' points to Jo from Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Anjou was a medieval French duchy on the Loire, later absorbed into the kingdom, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Asian should have Greek character encased in metal

indicators.note: a thing encased in something is wrapped all round by it

blocks.note: beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: Advice that an Asian ought to have a Greek letter set in metal, like a medallion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person from Greece, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Tibet, the Himalayan region, is Asian; the clue gives the nationality as a noun.

clue.text: Milk and old cake not finished

indicators.note: something not finished stops short, so its end is removed

blocks.note: ex- means former
a torte is a rich cake

explanation.surface: Milk and stale cake left half-eaten on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk' looks like the drink to go with the cake, but it is the verb meaning to exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk someone is to extract money from them by exploitation, which is what extorting by threats does.

clue.text: Medicines laid out across counter finally declared legal

indicators.note: things laid out are spread and rearranged, so these letters take a new order
finally points to the very end of the word it follows

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
the end of counter

explanation.surface: Medicines spread over a pharmacy counter are finally made legal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid' does double duty in the surface but is part of the fodder, with 'out' alone seeming spare; the rearranged letters lie across the final letter of the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Decriminalising a drug or act means ceasing to treat it as a criminal offence, making it legal in effect.

clue.text: Subordinate brought to northern river stays perhaps

blocks.note: one who is under another is subordinate
the Wear flows through Durham and Sunderland in north-east England

explanation.surface: A junior employee is taken up north to a river, where perhaps they stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' seems a verb, but stays are a corset, an old undergarment; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays were a boned corset worn beneath clothing, so they are one example of undergarments.

clue.text: Make quick note sailor’s wearing part of Highland dress

indicators.note: a garment being worn surrounds its wearer, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: to jot is to write a brief note
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor in Scottish costume, told to scribble a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'sailor's wearing' as 'sailor is worn by': the note wears the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A jabot is a lace frill at the throat worn with formal Scottish Highland evening dress.

clue.text: Pegasus perhaps wingless in beginning to catch space ship

indicators.note: without wings means both side extremities are lost
the beginning of a word is its first letter
one thing placed in others ends up enclosed by them

blocks.note: Pegasus is a winged horse; without its wings, the outer letters of horse drop
the first letter of catch
air is empty space

explanation.surface: Pegasus losing his wings while trying to catch a spaceship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space ship' pretends to be one thing; 'space' gives the letters and 'ship' is the definition. Pegasus perhaps is a horse, and wingless it drops both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a privateer or pirate, and the word also names the fast ship such a raider sailed.

clue.text: Important line as seen in Spielberg movie with soldiers

indicators.note: what is seen in something is inside it

blocks.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of, or as
E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial was directed by Steven Spielberg
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A key line of dialogue delivered in a Spielberg film full of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Important line' suggests a famous piece of film dialogue, but the line is geographical. OR, other ranks, is standard for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the most significant line of latitude, circling the globe midway between the poles.

clue.text: Rely on tanky at last coming in for start of union meeting

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it
coming in for something is taking its place, so one letter replaces another
the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to trust is to rely on
the end of tanky
the opening letter of union, the one replaced

explanation.surface: A hardline 'tanky' is finally trusted to open a union meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: A tankie is slang for a hardline communist, which lends the surface its trade-union flavour. The last letter of that word replaces the first of union.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a meeting, usually a secret romantic appointment between lovers.

clue.text: Cracked enigma involving a final letter in publication

indicators.note: a cracked code is broken apart and reassembled
to involve is to include within, so other letters are taken in

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle solved and printed, including the last letter, in a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked enigma' sounds like a code broken, as with the wartime Enigma machine; here it just scrambles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is a periodical publication containing articles and pictures, issued weekly or monthly.

clue.text: Wine unknown in cooler shown upside-down

indicators.note: in a down clue turning something upside-down makes it read bottom to top

blocks.note: algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
taken as written
a fan cools the air
to lead someone is to show them the way

explanation.surface: A wine bottle displayed upside-down in a cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' seems to be placing the unknown inside the cooler, but it is simply taken as written between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinfandel is a red grape widely grown in California and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Cutter‘s crew as before left at home

blocks.note: to man a ship is to crew it
do is short for ditto, the same as before
L is the abbreviation for left
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A boat's crew, as before, left at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' suggests a boat, fitting the crew, but it is the kitchen slicer, also spelt mandoline.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandolin in the kitchen is a frame with an adjustable blade for slicing vegetables thinly, so a cutter.

clue.text: Family servant kept rook in daughter’s place

indicators.note: being in someone's place means taking over their spot, so one letter replaces another

blocks.note: retained means kept
R is the chess notation for rook
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A household servant keeps a crow in the daughter's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' reads as the bird, but it is the chess piece, abbreviated R, and it swaps in for the D at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a servant who has worked for a family for many years, a word with a feudal ring.

clue.text: Attention drawn to collar and jewellery

blocks.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention
a collar is a ring round the neck

explanation.surface: Eyes are drawn to a collar and a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' reads as the part of a shirt, but here it is any band encircling something, a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring is an ornament worn on the ear lobe, one item of jewellery rather than jewellery as a mass.

clue.text: Line removed from ordinary Bellini work

indicators.note: taking something out of a word leaves the rest standing

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
normal means ordinary

explanation.surface: A line cut from a humdrum Bellini, the cocktail or the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Bellini sounds like the peach cocktail, but here it is Vincenzo Bellini, the Italian opera composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma, with its aria Casta diva, is the best-known opera by the composer Vincenzo Bellini.

clue.text: Comfort resistance woman tempted to swallow pork pie?

indicators.note: whatever swallows something holds it inside

blocks.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
Eve was tempted by the serpent in Eden
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, a porky

explanation.surface: Comforting someone whose resolve cracked at a tempting pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie; the question mark admits the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone's pain or distress is to ease it, which is one sense of comforting them.

clue.text: Harmony from A string with another note held

indicators.note: what is held is gripped inside something

blocks.note: taken as written
C is a musical note
cord is thin string

explanation.surface: Musical harmony from the A string, with another note sustained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A string' reads as a violin string tuned to A, and A is a note, hence 'another note'; but the A stands as itself and the string is a cord.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in accord is to be in agreement, the non-musical sense of harmony between people.

clue.text: Two dogs finding prune

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: A pair of hounds discovered chewing a dried plum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two dogs' asks for two words for dog: one noun, a mongrel, and one verb, to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune spending is to cut it back, which is what curtailing means.

clue.text: Improvised short excuse to involve Democrat

indicators.note: cut short means the end is lopped off
to involve something is to take it in

blocks.note: an alibi is an excuse proving absence
D stands for Democrat

explanation.surface: A politician's hastily made-up excuse drags in a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' clips the last letter from the excuse before the Democrat's letter goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad-lib remark is made up on the spot, without preparation, so it is improvised.

clue.text: Titled woman about to take in French island sent message

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way
to take something in is to hold it inside

blocks.note: Dame is a title for a woman honoured in Britain
île is French for island

explanation.surface: A lady about to visit a French island has sent word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' turns the woman round and 'to take in' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To email is to send an electronic message, so the past tense matches 'sent message'.

clue.text: Love upset where learner moves across college

indicators.note: a letter shifting to a new position changes the word's order

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, O
to rile is to upset

explanation.surface: Heartbreak as a student transfers to another college.
explanation.walkthrough: The learner is L, which hops one place to the right in the word for upset. Oriel is an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel College is one of the constituent colleges of Oxford University, founded in 1326.

clue.text: Veronica fit to join expedition

blocks.note: expedition in its old sense means promptness or speed
fit and well both mean healthy

explanation.surface: Veronica is healthy enough to go on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Veronica looks like a woman's name, but it is the botanical genus. 'Expedition' means haste here, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is the common name for plants of the genus Veronica, with small blue flowers.

clue.text: Dodgy boss nearly murdered lackey

indicators.note: nearly all means just short of complete, so the final letter goes
something murdered is mangled, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
boss with its last letter clipped

explanation.surface: A crooked boss all but killed his underling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'murdered' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is a British term for a drudge who does menial jobs for others, much like a lackey.

clue.text: Tragedian Edward‘s name on marble

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another is placed after it

blocks.note: an alley or ally is a large playing marble
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An Elizabethan actor's name carved on marble.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after. Edward Alleyn was the Elizabethan tragic actor who founded Dulwich College.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Alleyn was the leading tragic actor of Marlowe's day, famous as Faustus and Tamburlaine.
